_comment: Expected schema of a loaded Project Hammer snapshot. Ingest asserts against this
and FAILS LOUDLY on any difference -- it never silently casts, coerces, or infers.
SCHEMA VERSION 2 (2026-11-16). raw.nowtime changed from VARCHAR to BIGINT.
* What changed: upstream's SQLite now declares `nowtime INTEGER` (was TEXT) and stores
the observation date as digits, YYYYMMDD (20261104), where it used to store the
string 'YYYY-MM-DD'. It is a calendar date, not an epoch, and it has no time of day.
The change is archive-wide: every historical row is an integer too.
* When: first seen by the schema gate on 2026-11-06. The last archive in the old form
was the one refreshed on 2026-11-05 (upstream stamp 2026-11-04 17:02:49.08 Eastern).
The gate refused every run from 2026-11-06 until this file was updated.
* Upstream did NOT announce this change. It was caught by the gate, not by notice.
* Evidence and the proof of the decode: docs/incident-nowtime-type-change.md.
* Version 1 is kept as config/expected_schema.v1.json. The snapshots retained under
old form and are checked against it:
python scripts/check_schema.py --db <db> --schema config/expected_schema.v1.json
KNOWN PENDING CHANGE, STILL NOT LANDED: the maintainer has stated that raw.product_id
will change from a string to a number, to reduce SQLite file size. As of the archive
this version was captured from it is still VARCHAR. When that change lands, this file
is updated in its own commit with a note -- deliberately, never as a side effect of a
failing run -- and the current content is kept as expected_schema.v2.json.
Types are DuckDB type names as reported by information_schema.columns after
scripts/load_snapshot.py has copied the SQLite tables in.
